Captured outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/verify-image.txt: the `-- signature` block lists only 'The cosign claims were validated', transparency-log and certificate checks; no commit.

GitHub docs: attestations include "A link to the workflow associated with the artifact" and "The repository, organization, environment, commit SHA, and triggering event for the artifact." The container provenance example passes only subject-name, subject-digest and push-to-registry.

Round 2: claim narrowed to the round-1 suggested text. Stage-3 capture: the decoded payload yields `built by https://github.com/duyan11110/don-hang, .github/workflows/ci.yml at commit ... (push)`, i.e. keys repository, path, gitCommit and event_name are present (greps on verify-image.sh lines 40-46).

GitHub: "Public repositories that generate artifact attestations use the Sigstore Public Good Instance." OIDC reference: "Without `id-token: write`, the OIDC JWT ID token cannot be requested." Sigstore: Fulcio "signs X.509 certificates valid for 10 minutes." GitHub how-to example sets `id-token: write` and `attestations: write`.

Workflow syntax: "`attestations: write` permits an action to generate an artifact attestation for a build." Artifact attestations: "A copy of the generated Sigstore bundle is stored with GitHub". Push to ghcr.io with push-to-registry: true is shown by execution: Cosign finds the provenance in the registry in the stage-3 capture. Lesson §4 now matches this wording.

Execution: verify-image.sh line 37 passes the same `trusted` array (--certificate-identity https://github.com/duyan11110/don-hang/.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/master, --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com) and the stage-3 capture prints `-- provenance` / `built by https://github.com/duyan11110/don-hang, .github/workflows/ci.yml ... (push)` / `verified`.

GitHub (fetched 2026-10-14): "Artifact attestations by itself provides SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2." "Reusable workflows can provide isolation between the build process and the calling workflow" ... "to achieve SLSA v1 Build Level 3". ci.yml at stage-3 attests directly in the publish job (lines 278-296), no reusable workflow. Idea correct; the claim and §4 drop the "v1.0" GitHub attaches to the level.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: GitHub states that its artifact attestations alone reach SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2, and that Build Level 3 needs the build isolated from the calling workflow (for example in a reusable workflow); ci.yml attests inside the publish job itself, so Đơn Hàng stands at Build Level 2.

claim_verdicts.evidence: ci.yml at stage-3: both attest steps (lines 283, 291) set `create-storage-record: false`; the stage-3 capture of verify-image.sh ends the first block with `verified`.

GitHub OIDC: "A step or action in the workflow job can request a token from GitHub's OIDC provider"; without `id-token: write` the token "cannot be requested" (publish grants it, ci.yml line 224). Claim 6 (execution) shows a certificate from this job names ci.yml@refs/heads/master; verify-image.sh accepts any attestation under those flags and checks only repository/path text inside it (lines 37-42). GitHub ties Build L3 to isolating the build from the calling workflow.

The --type slsaprovenance1 + identity flags combination is settled by execution: the stage-3 capture of line 37 yields a decoded statement and `verified`. The new Base64 gloss in §5 is definitional. Capture: `== ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api:1.0.0 -> ...@sha256:1d0825...` / `-- signature` / `Error: no signatures found` / `not verified: refused`; no `-- provenance` line, consistent with `cosign verify ... || return 1` on line 31 returning before line 36.

Claim rewritten to a script fact. verify-image.sh line 31 passes only the `trusted` array to cosign verify: --certificate-identity (ci.yml@refs/heads/master) and --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com (lines 19-21); nothing else from the certificate is read. §6 now hedges the certificate contents ("Whatever else the keyless certificate records").

GitHub: "It is important to remember that artifact attestations are not a guarantee that an artifact is secure. Instead, artifact attestations link you to the source code and the build instructions that produced them."
GitHub: "The SLSA framework is an industry standard used to evaluate supply chain security." ci.yml at stage-3 contains no SLSA step; provenance comes from actions/attest-build-provenance.

Claim and §7 answer now follow the round-1 suggested text. verify() runs cosign verify with the `trusted` flags and `|| return 1` (line 31) before line 37; set -euo pipefail (line 5) makes a failed cosign in line 37's pipeline reach line 39's message. The publish job signs with its own identity (ci.yml line 276 `cosign sign --yes`), so a copy's image fails line 31 first.

issues.text: New in round 2 (replaces the round-1 major on SLSA levels, whose L1/L3 definitions are now cut). §4, summary line 5 and q5 relay GitHub's statement but drop the spec version GitHub gives: "SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2". Level numbering differs across SLSA versions.
issues.quote: GitHub states that its attestations alone reach SLSA Build Level 2, and that Level 3 needs more isolation of the build.
issues.fix: Once the owner adds standards.slsa to versions.yaml (open_question 1), write "SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2" in §4, summary line 5 and q5 explanation `correct`. Until then leave as is: the sentence is attributed to GitHub.

issues.text: New in round 2, in the rewritten SLSA paragraph. "more isolation of the build" does not say isolated from what. I can guess it from the next sentence (steps can get the ID token), but the two sentences are not tied together, so I re-read them twice.
issues.quote: and that Level 3 needs more isolation of the build. Đơn Hàng's is L2: any step in the `publish` job could ask for the same ID token
issues.fix: Replace "more isolation of the build" with "the build's steps kept away from the signing", so the next sentence reads as the reason Đơn Hàng misses it.

issues.text: New in round 2. q5 option d's explanation opens with "L2 means GitHub's own action signs the provenance". The lesson never says what L2 means, only that GitHub says its attestations reach it, so this reads as a new definition and makes me doubt my answer.
issues.quote: L2 means GitHub's own action signs the provenance, which sounds like protection against the job.
